boundary_rationale: Where the Aramaic sentence just before it argues from what the nations' gods did not do, this unit pivots to what Yahweh did do: a participial hymn opening, עֹשֵׂ֥ה אֶ֨רֶץ֙ בְּכֹח֔וֹ (oshb:Jer.10.12, byte), matching “God has made the earth by his power.” (web:Jer.10.12). The register shift out of the Aramaic citation formula that closed the previous verse (web:Jer.10.11) into a Hebrew creation doxology marks the edge; nothing internal to verses 12-16 breaks the hymn again. It closes on the name-formula, יְהוָ֥ה צְבָא֖וֹת שְׁמֽוֹ (oshb:Jer.10.16, byte) — “Yahweh of Armies is his name.” (web:Jer.10.16) — byte-identical to the same formula closing oshb:Jer.51.19, the closing verse of this hymn's twin at Jer.51.15-Jer.51.19; the wider twin pairing is held here as texture rather than as the warrant for this edge, and it does not hold at a single tier throughout — two of the five paired verses are byte-identical (oshb:Jer.10.12 and oshb:Jer.51.15; oshb:Jer.10.15 and oshb:Jer.51.18) while the other three diverge already in their consonants.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Folding this hymn into the surrounding polemic as one larger row was rejected because the participial hymn-opening and the shift out of the Aramaic citation formula are a sharper register break than anything inside the polemic itself, and the hymn is a bounded, self-closing unit with its own twin elsewhere in the book.

device_notes: oshb:Jer.10.11's setumah (WLC, single-witness, tier-3) marks the seam just ahead of this unit's own opening, and a further setumah closes the unit at oshb:Jer.10.16 — both texture, neither a driver. A ketiv/qere note sits inside this span at oshb:Jer.10.13, ketiv ארץ against qere הָאָ֑רֶץ (WLC, single-witness), both forms standing in the source bytes there with neither preferred as a reading. The definite article distinguishing those two forms is not recoverable from either witness's English: the same rendering, “from the ends of the earth” (web:Jer.10.13), also stands over the unrelated article-less parallel at web:Jer.51.16, so the wording favors neither form specifically. The name-formula closing verse 16 is byte-identical to the same formula closing the doxology's twin, Jer.51.15-Jer.51.19, held here as cross-book texture rather than as the boundary's warrant; three of the twin's five paired verses diverge in their consonants at or below skeleton tier.

boundary_rationale: A second-person feminine command opens the unit, אִסְפִּ֥י מֵאֶ֖רֶץ כִּנְעָתֵ֑ךְ (oshb:Jer.10.17, byte), matching “Gather up your wares out of the land, you who live under siege.” (web:Jer.10.17), addressed to the besieged city rather than to the idol-worshippers of the preceding hymn; the same verse carries a ketiv/qere note on the feminine participle naming that addressee (WLC, single-witness), read further below. A koh-amar clause follows at once, כִּֽי כֹה֙ אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֔ה (oshb:Jer.10.18, byte) — “Behold, I will sling out the inhabitants of the land at this time, and will distress them, that they may feel it.” (web:Jer.10.18) — joined to the command by an explicit because rather than opening a fresh address, so it is held inside the same unit rather than cut into its own row. Verses 19-21 shift, carrying no formula of their own, into a first-person cry of pain and a shepherds' indictment, and verse 22 closes on a report of a commotion out of the north, ק֤וֹל שְׁמוּעָה֙ (oshb:Jer.10.22, byte) — “The voice of news, behold, it comes, and a great commotion out of the north country,” (web:Jer.10.22). Those internal turns do not carry a koh-amar onset, an addressee change, or a discourse imperative of their own, so the whole stretch from the command through the report is held as one unit; the row is cut before verse 23 because that verse turns the address around, from a report about the coming danger to direct prayer speech to Yahweh.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Cutting a fresh row at the koh-amar clause in verse 18 was rejected because it is bound to verse 17's command by an explicit causal because rather than by any addressee change, and the unmarked turn into a first-person voice at verse 19 was held on the same ground rather than treated as its own seam.
literature_type_guess: siege announcement with an embedded cry of pain and shepherds' indictment

device_notes: A setumah closes the preceding span at oshb:Jer.10.16 (WLC, single-witness, tier-3), just before this unit's own opening command. A setumah recurs at oshb:Jer.10.17, oshb:Jer.10.18, oshb:Jer.10.21, and oshb:Jer.10.22 (WLC, single-witness, tier-3), not driving the internal turns disclosed above. A ketiv/qere note also sits at oshb:Jer.10.17 itself, ketiv ישבתי against qere יֹשֶׁ֖בֶת (WLC, single-witness) — the qere reads the addressee as the city who dwells under siege, matching the feminine command that opens the unit. Verses 19-21's first-person voice and the shepherds' indictment are held here as texture inside the unit rather than promoted to their own row, honestly short of certainty.

boundary_rationale: The second person turns from Yahweh, addressed throughout the preceding complaint, onto the prophet himself: כִּ֣י אֶת רַגְלִ֥ים רַ֨צְתָּה֙ וַיַּלְא֔וּךָ וְאֵ֥יךְ תְּתַֽחֲרֶ֖ה אֶת הַסּוּסִ֑ים (oshb:Jer.12.5, byte), matching “If you have run with the footmen, and they have wearied you, then how can you contend with horses?” (web:Jer.12.5), reading as Yahweh's own reply to the complaint just voiced. The reply closes with a warning against Jeremiah's own household, אַל תַּאֲמֵ֣ן בָּ֔ם כִּֽי יְדַבְּר֥וּ אֵלֶ֖יךָ טוֹבֽוֹת (oshb:Jer.12.6, byte) — “Don't believe them, though they speak beautiful words to you.” (web:Jer.12.6) — bringing in Jeremiah's own brothers and father's house as the participants in view, אַחֶ֣יךָ וּבֵית אָבִ֗יךָ (oshb:Jer.12.6, byte), a set standing nowhere in the complaint just addressed to Yahweh. The row is cut before verse 7 because the voice there turns again, to Yahweh speaking of forsaking my house rather than replying to Jeremiah.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Reading verses 5-6 as a continuation of Jeremiah's own complaint rather than Yahweh's reply was rejected because the addressee is named in the second person across both verses as the one who runs, whose brothers and father's house are in view — Jeremiah's own circumstances rather than Yahweh's.
literature_type_guess: Yahweh's reply to the complaint, warning against Jeremiah's own household
wj_or_red_letter_considered: not applicable in the OT substrate
device_notes: A setumah closes this short span at oshb:Jer.12.6 (WLC, single-witness, tier-3 corroboration), texture rather than a driver for the boundary; the two-verse span is held at reduced confidence honestly rather than forced to a firmer reading. A paseq mark is recorded at oshb:Jer.12.5, entered as a single-witness bare count only, with no position within the verse asserted. A treachery catchword straddles the seam between Jer.12.4 and Jer.12.5: the construct participle כָּל בֹּ֥גְדֵי בָֽגֶד closes oshb:Jer.12.1 (byte tier; that form: 1 verse at byte tier, 1 verse at accent-stripped tier), and the finite verb בָּ֣גְדוּ בָ֔ךְ stands at oshb:Jer.12.6 (byte tier; that form: 1 verse at byte tier, 2 verses at accent-stripped tier — MT 5:11 and MT 12:6); it is disclosed rather than treated as a seam-deleter, since the addressee-and-participant shift at the seam is the controlling ground for the cut.

boundary_rationale: A koh-amar clause turns the address outward to the neighboring nations, כֹּ֣ה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֗ה (oshb:Jer.12.14, byte), matching “Yahweh says,” (web:Jer.12.14), opening a declaration against those who touch the heritage just lamented, הִנְנִ֤י נֹֽתְשָׁם֙ מֵעַ֣ל אַדְמָתָ֔ם (oshb:Jer.12.14, byte) — “Behold, I will pluck them up from off their land,” (web:Jer.12.14) — rather than the heritage itself. A promise of compassion for Jacob and a conditional blessing for the neighbors who learn Jacob's ways are folded into the same speech rather than opening fresh units of their own — an operative judgment-oracle reading is kept for the whole four verses, with the restoration content disclosed here rather than given a separate label, since the unit opens and closes on uprooting language and the compassion clause is grammatically subordinate to it. The unit, and the chapter, close on the closing-speech formula, נְאֻם יְהוָֽה (oshb:Jer.12.17, byte), matching “says Yahweh.” (web:Jer.12.17), the clause immediately before it reading, “But if they will not hear, then I will pluck up that nation, plucking up and destroying it,” (web:Jer.12.17); a fresh command opens immediately afterward at web:Jer.13.1, corroborating the close read here.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Splitting the restoration promise in verses 15-16 out of the judgment envelope that opens and closes the unit was rejected because that promise is grammatically subordinate to the uprooting announced in verse 14, introduced by after I have plucked them up rather than by any independent formula.
literature_type_guess: judgment on the neighboring nations with a conditional promise of restoration

device_notes: A setumah closes the preceding span at oshb:Jer.12.13 (WLC, single-witness, tier-3), just before this unit's own opening koh-amar; a further setumah closes the unit and the chapter at oshb:Jer.12.17, the same verse as the closing-speech formula named above, disclosed here as texture rather than as its warrant. A paseq mark is recorded at oshb:Jer.12.14, entered as a single-witness bare count only, with no position within the verse asserted. Labeling the whole four verses judgment_oracle rather than splitting off a salvation_oracle for the restoration clause is a per-bytes operative-category choice, held short of certainty given how substantial that clause is.

boundary_rationale: A fresh commissioning clause opens the row: “Therefore you shall speak to them this word” (web:Jer.13.12), spliced וְאָמַרְתָּ֨ אֲלֵיהֶ֜ם אֶת הַדָּבָ֣ר הַזֶּ֗ה (oshb:Jer.13.12, byte tier) -- a waw-prefixed suffix-conjugation form rather than a morphological imperative, Yahweh commissioning Jeremiah to relay a new saying to a broad audience, distinct from the belt’s own interpretation just given. The identical opening run recurs inside the span at “Then tell them” (web:Jer.13.13), וְאָמַרְתָּ֨ אֲלֵיהֶ֜ם (oshb:Jer.13.13, byte tier; that pointed run, sweep: 4 verses), continuing the same commissioned speech to the same audience rather than opening a second unit. The commissioned proverb, “Every container should be filled with wine” (web:Jer.13.12), turns into a judgment against “the kings who sit on David’s throne, the priests, the prophets, and all the inhabitants of Jerusalem” (web:Jer.13.13). The neum-YHWH formula stands inside 13:14 at the accent break, נְאֻם יְהוָ֑ה (oshb:Jer.13.14, byte tier), not at the verse’s end: two further negated clauses continue afterward to the verse’s own close, “I will not pity, spare, or have compassion, that I should not destroy them” (web:Jer.13.14). The unit’s actual close is corroborated by the fresh imperative address opening next at 13:15.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Folding this proverb-oracle into the preceding sign-act row was considered: both concern the same belt-owning voice, but 13:12 opens its own commissioned-speech clause addressed to a wider audience rather than continuing the belt's interpretation, so the two stay separate.
literature_type_guess: riddle-proverb turned judgment oracle: wine-jars saying applied to national drunkenness

device_notes: Jer.13.12 carries a setumah, and Jer.13.14, this unit's own close, carries a further setumah; the WLC records it as a single-witness mark whose tier-3 standing draws weak support from the Prophets.

boundary_rationale: “Hear, and give ear” (web:Jer.13.15), rendering שִׁמְע֥וּ וְהַאֲזִ֖ינוּ (oshb:Jer.13.15, byte tier), opens a fresh imperative address to the audience distinct from the commissioned proverb just closed. The call to give Yahweh glory before darkness falls (13:16) shifts in 13:17 into first-person prophetic grief -- “my soul will weep in secret for your pride” -- without any addressee or scene change, so the weeping stays inside this warning rather than opening a fresh unit.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Labeling this row lament_confession on the strength of 13:17’s first-person weeping was considered and set aside: the second-person-plural verb וְאִם֙ לֹ֣א תִשְׁמָע֔וּהָ (oshb:Jer.13.17, byte tier) keeps the weeping inside an address to the plural audience running from 13:15, not a petition addressed to Yahweh.
literature_type_guess: warning oracle with embedded prophetic weeping over threatened exile
wj_or_red_letter_considered: not applicable in the OT substrate
device_notes: The setumah standing at oshb:Jer.13.14 sits immediately ahead of this unit's own opening; Jer.13.17, the row's own close, carries a second setumah (WLC, single-witness, tier-3 in the Prophets). Jer.13.16, inside the span, carries one further note in the same single-witness inventory, the unpointed ketiv ישית beside the pointed qere וְשִׁ֖ית (oshb:Jer.13.16, byte tier). Yahweh’s flock closing this row at עֵ֥דֶר יְהוָֽה (oshb:Jer.13.17, byte tier) returns as הָעֵ֨דֶר֙ (oshb:Jer.13.20, byte tier), that consonantal noun standing at 6 verses book-wide (sweep: 6 verses); the cut nonetheless holds because a fresh discourse imperative reopens the address to the king and the queen mother at 13:18, a distinct addressee pair from the plural audience carried through 13:15-17.

boundary_rationale: A new address opens at 13:20, though not immediately in the feminine singular: “Lift up your eyes, and see those who come from the north” (web:Jer.13.20) renders שאי שְׂא֤וּ עֵֽינֵיכֶם֙ וראי וּרְא֔וּ הַבָּאִ֖ים מִצָּפ֑וֹן (oshb:Jer.13.20, byte tier), a doubled-note verse whose two opening imperatives each carry a ketiv/qere pair -- feminine singular on the ketiv, masculine plural on the qere -- with the intervening object עֵֽינֵיכֶם֙ taking a masculine-plural suffix under either reading. The feminine-singular Jerusalem address itself begins only with לָ֔ךְ and תִּפְאַרְתֵּֽךְ later in the same verse, and governs from there through the closing vocative at 13:27, distinct from the king-and-queen-mother pair addressed just before. The sustained indictment of Jerusalem-as-woman runs through the scattering sentence (13:24-25) and the uncovering of her skirts (13:26) to the closing apostrophe: “Woe to you, Jerusalem” (web:Jer.13.27), where א֥וֹי לָךְ֙ יְר֣וּשָׁלִַ֔ם (oshb:Jer.13.27, byte tier) is the oy lexeme (sweep: 8 verses book-wide) -- a different word from the bare hoy, ה֣וֹי (oshb:Jer.22.13 and oshb:Jer.23.1, byte tier), that opens the woe oracles at 22:13 and 23:1; the vav-prefixed shape, וְה֣וֹי (oshb:Jer.22.18, byte tier), stands here and, in its own pointing, again at 34:5 (sweep: 2 verses), both funeral cries, so this row is not typed woe_oracle. The span’s own divine formula is the neum-YHWH at 13:25, נְאֻם יְהוָ֑ה (oshb:Jer.13.25, byte tier), not a koh-amar: the chapter’s four koh-amar sites, 13:1, 13:9, 13:12 and 13:13, all stand before this row opens. Jer.13.27, this unit's own closing verse, carries no closure formula of its own: the neum-YHWH stands at oshb:Jer.13.25, inside the span rather than at its close, and the unit closes instead on the apostrophe already carried in that verse's own bytes, oshb:Jer.13.27 (byte tier).
strongest_rejected_alternative: Joining 13:20-27 to the preceding royal oracle (13:18-19) into one ten-verse row was considered: the shift from the royal pair's plural address to the feminine-singular Jerusalem address that governs from mid-13:20 is real, but the two share the same humiliation-and-exposure imagery, so the fold-together reading is not unreasonable.
literature_type_guess: Jerusalem-as-adulteress indictment closing in a funeral-toned apostrophe

device_notes: Jer.13.19 carries a setumah just ahead of this row’s opening; Jer.13.27, this unit's own closing verse, carries a petuchah; the WLC records it too as a single-witness mark, its tier-3 standing drawing weak support from the Prophets. Two catchwords reach back across the opening seam: תִּֽפְאַרְתְּכֶֽם (oshb:Jer.13.18, byte tier), closing 13:18, recurs inside this row’s own opening verse as תִּפְאַרְתֵּֽךְ (oshb:Jer.13.20, byte tier; that stem, sweep: 4 verses), and עֵ֥דֶר (oshb:Jer.13.17, byte tier), closing 13:17, recurs here as הָעֵ֨דֶר֙ (oshb:Jer.13.20, byte tier; that noun, sweep: 6 verses); the cut before this row still holds because 13:20’s own doubled-note imperatives and masculine-plural object open a fresh address that the shared imagery alone does not erase.

boundary_rationale: “This is Yahweh’s word that came to Jeremiah concerning the drought” (web:Jer.14.1) renders the full header, אֲשֶׁ֨ר הָיָ֤ה דְבַר יְהוָה֙ אֶֽל יִרְמְיָ֔הוּ עַל דִּבְרֵ֖י הַבַּצָּרֽוֹת (oshb:Jer.14.1, byte tier) -- the OAN/topical-header shape, attested at four sites book-wide (sweep: 4 verses: 14:1, 46:1, 47:1, 49:34). The header is kept with the drought description that follows (14:2-6: mourning gates, dry cisterns, cracked ground, the doe forsaking her fawn, the wild donkeys panting) rather than standing alone: no addressee or scene shift separates the title from what it introduces, and at the other three sites the same header shape carries its own attached content rather than standing bare -- 46:1 heads the whole nations collection, while 47:1 and 49:34 each head a single-nation oracle with its own attached setting. Framed here as judgment_oracle by its dominant content -- a report of covenant devastation already unfolding -- rather than superscription, since only one of the six verses is the bare title.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Isolating 14:1 as its own one-verse superscription row, separate from the drought description, was considered and set aside in favor of the larger bundled unit, since the description carries the row's substance and no addressee shift separates the header from what it introduces.
literature_type_guess: topical word-event header opening a drought-devastation report

The petuchah at oshb:Jer.13.27 stands immediately ahead of this unit's own opening (single-witness, tier-3 WLC corroboration in the Prophets); no verse within 14:1-6 itself carries a parashah mark.
